FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Milling 
Cutters, Saws, Gear Cutting Tools and Broaches Sectional Committee had been approved by the Production 
Engineering Division Council. 

This standard has been prepared on the basis of experience gained at national level and development at 
international level. 

Other standards in this series are: 

IS 14584 ; 1998 Spline and serration hobs — Technical supply conditions 
IS 10608 : 1998 Spline hob — Straight sided — Specification (first revision) 
IS 14585 : 1998 Spline hob — Involute sided — Specification 

Other related standards are: 

IS 8731 : 1978 Technical supply conditions for general purpose gear hobs 

IS 8732 : 1978 Single start gear hobs with axial key way 

IS 8733 : 1978 Tolerances for single start gear hobs 



IS 14586 : 1998 



Indian Standard 

SERRATION HOBS — STRAIGHT SIDED — 

SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

This standard covers the dimensions and requirements 
for straight sided serration hobs, suitable for serrations 
according to IS 3654:1966 'Dimensions for straight 

sided serrations'. 

2 REFERENCES 

The following Indian Standards contain provisions 
which through reference in this text, constitute 
provision of this standard. At the time of publication, 
the editions indicated were valid. All standards are 
subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on 
this standard are encouraged to investigate the 
possibility of applying the most recent editions of the 
standards indicated below: 

IS No. Title 

3654 : 1966 Dimensions for straight sided serra- 

tions 

14584 : 1998 Spline and serration hobs — Tech- 
nical supply conditions 

8733 : 197£ Tolerances for single start gear hobs 

3 DIMENSIONS 

The dimensions of straight sided serration hobs are 
given in Table 1. 



4 ACCURACY 

The accuracy for straight sided serration hobs shall be 
as given in IS 8733. 

5 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 

5.1 For other requirements not covered in this 
standard, IS 14584 shall apply. 

53, Gashing may be done preferably in perpendicular 
direction and in opposite helix of hob thread, when 
setting angle for hobbing (lead angle of thread) is more 
than 3 degrees. This gashing may also be parallel to 
hob axis and marked with symbol (infinity) for the 
gash lead and setting angle for sharpening is zero 
degree. 

5.3 It is recommended to follow basic profile II for the 
serrations of size from 7 mm x 8 mm to 30 mm x 34 mm 
according to IS 3654 to simplify the manufacturing of 
such serration hobs. 

6 DESIGNATION 

A straight sided serration hob with right hand thread 
to cut serrations of size 45 mm x 50 mm according to 
IS 3654 with basic profile I and grade of accuracy 'A', 
made of high speed steel and confirming to this 
standard shall be designated as: 

Straight sided serration hob IS 14586 I — A 45 x 50 



IS 14586 : 1998

{Clause 3) 
All dimensions in millimetres.

NOTE — The dimensions of hub diameter *d\ ' are left to the manufacturer's discretion. This diameter shall be as large as possible and 
greater than the spacing ring. Hub diameter may be conical or cylindrical. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and 
attending to connected matters in the country* 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form 
without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of 
implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. 
Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publication), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue 
of *BIS Handbook* and 'Standards Monthly Additions' 

This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc: No. PE 11 ( 5319 ).
